points_of_disagreement: Whether the attack should be labeled 'terrorism' or 'resistance' — a fundamental disagreement about legitimacy and framing
Whether the attacker's actions were primarily individually motivated or structurally caused by occupation and cycle of violence
Whether Ben-Gvir's response represents appropriate security leadership or political exploitation of tragedy
Whether the IDF's subsequent West Bank operations constitute justified security measures or collective punishment
Whether the death penalty law should be applied and whether it targets Palestinians discriminatorily
Whether the attack reflects a new internal security threat (Arab-Israeli citizens) or is continuous with existing patterns
Whether the attack should be contextualized within broader Israeli-Palestinian violence or treated as a discrete criminal/security incident
shared_foundation.summary: All framings agree on the concrete facts: an Arab Israeli citizen carried out a multi-location shooting in central Israel, killing one person (Haim Kalomiti) and injuring five others, before being killed by police. The disagreements are entirely interpretive: whether this was terrorism or resistance, individually motivated or structurally caused, and how Israel should respond—questions that reflect deeper disputes about occupation, security, rule of law, and the legitimacy of political violence.

framings.name: Terrorism / Security Threat
framings.question: Was this a terrorist attack, and did Israeli security forces respond effectively?
framings.key_claim: An Arab Israeli carried out a premeditated, nationally-motivated terrorist shooting spree, and Israeli security forces neutralized the threat swiftly.
framings.description: This framing centers on the attack as an act of terrorism against Israeli civilians and soldiers, emphasizing the attacker's identity, the multi-site coordination, and the police response. It foregrounds the victim — IDF reservist Haim Kalomiti — as a hero who died defending his community.
framings.emphasizes: The terrorist designation, the attacker's identity as an Arab Israeli citizen, the heroism of security forces and the victim, the multi-site nature of the attack as evidence of planning.
framings.downplays: Broader geopolitical context, the attacker's possible motivations, or the conditions in the West Bank that may have contributed.
sample_headlines: 1 dead, 5 wounded in shooting spree in central Israel; terrorism suspected
Israeli man killed, five hurt in central Israel terror shooting spree by Arab Israeli

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: An Arab Israeli terrorist opened fire in several locations in a shooting spree in central Israel on Sunday
carriers.role_evidence: Among the first English-language outlets to use 'terrorist' in the headline and frame the event as a nationally-motivated attack.

carriers.name: World Israel News
carriers.excerpt: Six people were shot at three different locations by Israeli Arab terrorist
carriers.role_evidence: Adopted the terrorism framing immediately and prominently in its headline and lede.

carriers.name: Ynet News
carriers.excerpt: Police say suspicions were growing that the attack was nationally motivated
carriers.role_evidence: Major Israeli English-language outlet amplifying the terrorism/national motivation framing to a broad international audience.

carriers.name: Jerusalem Post
carriers.excerpt: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel is 'fighting a war on all fronts' following the terror attack
carriers.role_evidence: Widely-read outlet that amplified official Israeli government framing of the event as terrorism.

carriers.name: Israeli Police Commissioner Daniel Levy
carriers.excerpt: Israeli police commissioner Daniel Levy referred to the series of attacks as a 'killing spree'
carriers.role_evidence: Top law enforcement official officially designated the event a terror attack, lending institutional weight to this framing.

carriers.name: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
carriers.excerpt: Netanyahu said Israel is 'fighting a war on all fronts' following the terror attack
carriers.role_evidence: Head of government officially adopted the terrorism framing and praised security forces, cementing it as the state's position.

framings.name: Political Exploitation / Far-Right Opportunism
framings.question: Is the Israeli far-right using this attack to advance a pre-existing political agenda, including the death penalty law?
framings.key_claim: Far-right minister Ben-Gvir exploited the attack to promote his death penalty law and stage a political spectacle, raising concerns about the weaponization of tragedy.
framings.description: This framing focuses on how Israeli politicians — especially National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir — immediately leveraged the attack to push for the death penalty for terrorists and to score political points, including posting a video next to the blurred image of the dead gunman.
framings.emphasizes: Ben-Gvir's video and statements, the death penalty law's contested status, the political theater surrounding the response, condemnation from other Israeli leaders.
framings.downplays: The security response itself, the victim's story, or the broader conflict context.
sample_headlines: Ben-Gvir Pushes for Executions after Multi-Site Shooting near Qalqilya
'This is the end of every terrorist': Ben-Gvir posts video next to blurred image of dead gunman

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: Ben-Gvir released a video of himself standing next to what appeared to be a blurred image of the dead gunman
carriers.role_evidence: AP wire story distributed widely, foregrounding Ben-Gvir's political behavior as a key element of the event's narrative.

carriers.name: Palestine Chronicle
carriers.excerpt: Ben-Gvir Pushes for Executions after Multi-Site Shooting near Qalqilya
carriers.role_evidence: Headline and framing center entirely on Ben-Gvir's political exploitation, amplifying this angle to a pro-Palestinian readership.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: 'This is an apartheid regime': Critics decry Israel's new death penalty law
carriers.role_evidence: Pre-existing Al Jazeera coverage of the death penalty law provides the critical context that this framing draws on when applied to the attack.

carriers.name: Itamar Ben-Gvir (X/Twitter)
carriers.excerpt: Whoever murders a Jew will see the hangman's noose
carriers.role_evidence: Ben-Gvir's own posts originated the political exploitation angle by immediately invoking the death penalty law and posting the controversial video.

framings.name: Cycle of Violence / Contextual Causation
framings.question: Is this attack a predictable consequence of escalating Israeli military operations and settler violence in the West Bank?
framings.key_claim: The shooting is inseparable from a broader cycle of violence, including Israeli settler attacks and the killing of a Palestinian baby in the West Bank days before.
framings.description: This framing situates the attack within the ongoing conflict, pointing to recent Israeli military operations, settler violence, and the killing of a Palestinian infant as context that helps explain — though not justify — the attack. It treats the event as one node in a feedback loop of violence.
framings.emphasizes: The West Bank violence surge, the killing of a Palestinian baby days prior, settler attacks, and the broader occupation as structural drivers.
framings.downplays: The individual agency of the attacker, the specific victims' stories, or Israeli security successes.
sample_headlines: Palestinian man with Israeli citizenship opens fire in central Israel, killing 1 and wounding 5
Gunman kills 1, wounds 5 in drive-by attacks in Israel near West Bank border

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: The attack came at a time of heightened tensions following a spate of Israeli settler attacks
carriers.role_evidence: AP's wire story explicitly contextualizes the attack within the settler violence and the killing of a Palestinian baby, originating this framing in mainstream English-language coverage.

carriers.name: CBC News
carriers.excerpt: A gunman in a car opened fire at three locations in Israel close to the border with the occupied West Bank
carriers.role_evidence: CBC's framing emphasizes proximity to the occupied West Bank and uses neutral language ('gunman' not 'terrorist'), situating the event in the conflict geography.

carriers.name: NBC News
carriers.excerpt: A 35-year-old man was killed and five others injured in a series of shootings near the occupied West Bank
carriers.role_evidence: Major US network outlet framing the event in relation to the occupied West Bank, amplifying the contextual causation lens to a broad American audience.

carriers.name: Hamas (official statement)
carriers.excerpt: Hamas praised the attack as 'a response to the ongoing Israeli aggression against the Gaza Strip'
carriers.role_evidence: Hamas officially framed the attack as a response to Israeli actions, adopting the cycle-of-violence narrative for its own political purposes.

carriers.name: Palestine Chronicle
carriers.excerpt: Palestinian factions described the operation as a response to ongoing genocide in Gaza and violence in the occupied West Bank
carriers.role_evidence: Amplifies the contextual causation framing by foregrounding Palestinian faction statements linking the attack to Israeli actions.

framings.name: Arab-Israeli Identity / Internal Security Threat
framings.question: What does it mean for Israeli national security that the attacker was an Arab citizen of Israel, not a West Bank Palestinian?
framings.key_claim: The fact that the attacker was an Israeli Arab citizen — not a West Bank infiltrator — exposes a new and unexpected dimension of Israel's internal security challenge.
framings.description: This framing focuses on the attacker's status as an Israeli citizen from Taybeh, highlighting the shock among Israeli officials and residents that the threat came from within Israel's own Arab community rather than from across the West Bank barrier. It raises questions about radicalization, community relations, and the limits of border security.
framings.emphasizes: The attacker's Israeli citizenship, the surprise of officials and residents, the inadequacy of border-focused security paradigms, and the implications for Arab-Jewish coexistence.
framings.downplays: The broader geopolitical conflict, the political response, or the victim's story.
sample_headlines: 'I don't think anyone imagined the attackers were Israeli citizens,' says regional council head
Gunman identified as Arab Israeli from Taybeh — not a West Bank infiltrator

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: 'I don't think that anyone imagined that we would discover the attackers were Israeli citizens'
carriers.role_evidence: AP story quotes the regional council head expressing shock at the attacker's Israeli citizenship, originating this framing in English-language coverage.

carriers.name: Ynet News
carriers.excerpt: Police said one suspect, identified as Arab Israeli, eliminated
carriers.role_evidence: Ynet's headline and coverage foreground the attacker's Arab Israeli identity as the defining characteristic of the event.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: Security officials identified the terrorist as Omar Yassin, an Israeli citizen in his 20s who resided in Tayibe
carriers.role_evidence: Widely-read outlet that amplified the attacker's Israeli citizenship as a key narrative element, reaching a large international audience.

carriers.name: Oshrit Gani Gonen (Regional Council Head)
carriers.excerpt: 'Since Oct. 7, the scenario we were expecting was terrorists crossing into our towns from over the boundary'
carriers.role_evidence: Local official's statement crystallized the internal-threat framing by articulating the gap between expected and actual threat vectors.

framings.name: Resistance / Anti-Occupation Narrative
framings.question: Was this a legitimate act of resistance against Israeli occupation and ongoing military violence?
framings.key_claim: Palestinian factions frame the shooting as a natural and heroic response to Israeli military aggression in Gaza and the West Bank, calling for further escalation.
framings.description: This framing, advanced by Palestinian militant groups and some pro-Palestinian media, characterizes the attack not as terrorism but as armed resistance to occupation, genocide, and settler violence. It celebrates the attacker and calls for more such actions.
framings.emphasizes: Israeli military operations in Gaza and the West Bank, settler violence, the killing of Palestinian civilians (including a baby), and the legitimacy of armed resistance.
framings.downplays: The Israeli victims' humanity, the attacker's targeting of civilians, or the legal/moral status of attacks on non-combatants.
sample_headlines: Abu Obeida Hails Kochav Yair Operation, Calls for Escalation across Palestine
Hamas: Shooting is 'a response to ongoing Israeli aggression against the Gaza Strip'

carriers.name: Hamas (official statement)
carriers.excerpt: Hamas praised 'the heroic' shooting attack, calling it 'a response to the ongoing Israeli aggression'
carriers.role_evidence: Hamas was the first major faction to publicly frame the attack as heroic resistance, originating this narrative.

carriers.name: Palestine Chronicle
carriers.excerpt: Several Palestinian resistance groups issued statements praising the operation
carriers.role_evidence: Pro-Palestinian outlet amplified statements from Hamas, Islamic Jihad, and other factions framing the attack as resistance.

carriers.name: Islamic Jihad / Al-Quds Brigades
carriers.excerpt: Islamic Jihad described the shooting as a natural response to Israeli actions against Palestinians
carriers.role_evidence: Palestinian Islamic Jihad officially adopted the resistance framing, lending it institutional weight alongside Hamas.

carriers.name: Popular Resistance Committees / Palestinian Mujahideen Movement
carriers.excerpt: The Popular Resistance Committees and others praised the operation and called for continued resistance activities
carriers.role_evidence: Multiple factions amplifying the resistance framing in coordinated statements broadened its reach across Palestinian political networks.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: Hamas said the shooting was 'a natural response to the crimes of the occupation'
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's coverage of similar prior attacks shows a pattern of reporting Palestinian faction statements framing attacks as resistance, providing context for this framing's amplification.

framings.name: Human Cost / Victim-Centered
framings.question: Who was killed and wounded, and what does their loss mean?
framings.key_claim: The human face of the attack is IDF reservist Haim Kalomiti, 55, a married father of three who died defending his community — and five others whose lives were upended.
framings.description: This framing centers the identities, lives, and losses of the specific victims rather than the political or security dimensions of the event. It humanizes the dead and wounded and focuses on grief, community impact, and the personal cost of violence.
framings.emphasizes: Kalomiti's biography, his role as a community defender, the injuries of the five wounded, the lockdown of children at school, and the grief of the community.
framings.downplays: The attacker's identity or motivations, the political fallout, or the broader conflict.
sample_headlines: Chief Sgt. First Class (res.) Haim Kalomiti, 55, killed in central Israel terror attack
Reservist killed while defending community; children locked down at school for three hours

carriers.name: Jerusalem Post
carriers.excerpt: Chief Sgt. First Class (res.) Haim Kalomiti, 55, killed in central Israel terror attack
carriers.role_evidence: Dedicated article naming and profiling the victim, originating the victim-centered framing in English-language coverage.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: Kalomiti, a married father of three, served in the IDF's Ephraim Regional Brigade
carriers.role_evidence: Widely-read outlet provided biographical detail on the victim, amplifying the human cost framing to a large international audience.

carriers.name: i24 News
carriers.excerpt: The IDF later named Master Sergeant (Res.) Haim Kalomiti as the victim killed in the attack
carriers.role_evidence: i24 was among the first to name the victim and detail his role as a regional defense soldier, amplifying the human cost angle.

carriers.name: Drom HaSharon Regional Council
carriers.excerpt: Kalomiti 'was killed while going out to save lives and worked extensively for the security of the State of Israel'
carriers.role_evidence: Local government body officially memorialized the victim, institutionalizing the human cost and heroism framing.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: Fears of a widespread attack prompted authorities to order residents to stay at home, and children were kept in lockdown at school for at least three hours
carriers.role_evidence: AP wire story distributed globally, foregrounding the community-level human impact including children in lockdown.

framings.name: Collective Punishment / Israeli Military Response
framings.question: Will Israel's military response — closures, raids, and encirclements — constitute collective punishment of Arab communities?
framings.key_claim: Israel's immediate military response — sealing off West Bank villages, raiding Taybeh, and encircling Palestinian communities — risks punishing entire populations for one individual's actions.
framings.description: This framing scrutinizes the Israeli military and police response to the attack, focusing on the closure of Palestinian villages, raids in Taybeh, and the broader pattern of collective punishment that follows such attacks. It raises legal and humanitarian concerns about proportionality.
framings.emphasizes: IDF encirclement of West Bank villages, raids in Taybeh, the pattern of collective punishment, and Palestinian civilian fears of retaliation.
framings.downplays: The security rationale for the response, the attack itself, or the victim's story.
sample_headlines: IDF places broad closure on Palestinian villages after Kochav Yair attack
Palestinians brace for collective punishment after central Israel shooting

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: Palestinians in the West Bank are preparing themselves to face collective punishment from Israel in retaliation for the attack
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's coverage of prior similar attacks establishes its pattern of originating the collective punishment framing, directly applicable here.

carriers.name: Jerusalem Post
carriers.excerpt: The IDF has placed a broad closure on Palestinian villages in the area and is conducting raids in Tayibe
carriers.role_evidence: Reports the military response factually, providing the raw material for the collective punishment framing without explicitly adopting it.

carriers.name: Times of Israel
carriers.excerpt: The IDF said it encircled several West Bank Palestinian villages in the area of Kochav Ya'ir and sealed off a nearby crossing into Israel
carriers.role_evidence: Reports the military encirclement factually; the framing is adopted more critically by other outlets.

carriers.name: NBC News
carriers.excerpt: Israeli soldiers were deployed to one of the sites in central Israel and to a nearby Israeli settlement in the West Bank after the shootings
carriers.role_evidence: Major US outlet reporting the military deployment in the context of the occupied West Bank, amplifying awareness of the response's geographic scope.

framings.name: Death Penalty Law / Rule of Law
framings.question: Does this attack validate or delegitimize Israel's newly passed death penalty law for terrorists?
framings.key_claim: The attack immediately became a political test case for Israel's contested new death penalty law, with Ben-Gvir demanding its enforcement and critics warning of discriminatory application.
framings.description: This framing treats the attack as a flashpoint for the debate over Israel's March 2026 death penalty law for terrorists, which applies in military courts and has been criticized as ethnically discriminatory. It asks whether the law will be enforced, challenged, or used as political theater.
framings.emphasizes: The death penalty law's passage, its legal challenges, Ben-Gvir's demands for enforcement, and critics' arguments that it targets Palestinians by ethnicity.
framings.downplays: The attack's immediate human toll, the security response, or the broader conflict context.
sample_headlines: 'This is precisely why Otzma Yehudit enacted the Death Penalty for Terrorists Law' — Ben-Gvir
'This is an apartheid regime': Critics decry Israel's new death penalty law

carriers.name: Itamar Ben-Gvir (X/Twitter)
carriers.excerpt: This is precisely why Otzma Yehudit enacted the Death Penalty for Terrorists Law
carriers.role_evidence: Ben-Gvir's own posts explicitly linked the attack to the death penalty law, originating this framing.

carriers.name: Jerusalem Post
carriers.excerpt: The controversial death penalty for terrorists law was passed by the Knesset in March
carriers.role_evidence: Provided context on the law's passage and contested status, amplifying the rule-of-law framing.

carriers.name: Al Jazeera English
carriers.excerpt: 'Fundamentally, this is an apartheid regime,' Yair Dvir from B'Tselem told Al Jazeera
carriers.role_evidence: Al Jazeera's prior deep-dive on the death penalty law provides the critical legal and rights-based framing that is now applied to this attack.

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / Associated Press
carriers.excerpt: Ben-Gvir recently led an effort to pass a new law that seeks to impose the death penalty on Palestinian attackers. That law faces legal challenges.
carriers.role_evidence: AP wire story distributed globally flagged the death penalty law and its legal challenges, amplifying this framing to a mainstream international audience.

carriers.name: B'Tselem (Israeli human rights organization)
carriers.excerpt: 'There are entire sets of laws that differentiate between Jews and Palestinians'
carriers.role_evidence: Israeli rights group providing the institutional critique of the death penalty law that critics apply to Ben-Gvir's post-attack statements.

gap_analysis: Missing are framings centered on: (1) Mental health/individual pathology explanations that depoliticize the shooter's motivations; (2) Gun control/weapons access policy perspectives; (3) Police use-of-force accountability and the circumstances of the shooter's death; (4) Comparative analysis of how similar incidents by different perpetrators receive differential media/legal treatment; (5) Community trauma and healing frameworks that don't center political narratives; (6) Economic marginalization or local grievance angles specific to the shooter's circumstances. The current map skews toward macro political/ideological frames while underrepresenting individual-level, procedural justice, and apolitical public health framings.
